translationRepairs: After the Xianfeng era, the Beijing Copper Bureau also handled collections.
From the Xianfeng era onward, the Beijing Copper Bureau also handled collections.

咸豐後 here continues the list of collection venues and marks time from the Xianfeng reign onward; the Beijing Copper Bureau began handling juan-na during Xianfeng, so “after the Xianfeng era” wrongly postpones the measure until after that reign ended.
In Yongzheng 12 (1734), the Henan grain-reserve transport purchase regulations were opened.
In Yongzheng 12 (1734), the advance grain-transport purchase regulations were opened.

豫籌糧運例 is the “advance planning of grain transport” purchase schedule (豫籌 = plan in advance). Reading 豫 as Henan and 籌 as grain-reserve invents a provincial scheme; the later 豫工例 is the distinct Henan works schedule.
In the twelfth year, the Henan grain-reserve transport regulations were opened.
In the twelfth year, the advance grain-transport regulations were opened.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 豫籌 as Henan grain-reserve. 豫籌 means planning in advance, not the province 豫.
An edict approved ranks up to central secretaries and compilers in the capital and sub-prefects and sub-circuit magistrates in the provinces, provided the regular route was not harmed.

An edict approved ranks from central secretaries, messengers, reviewers, and doctors downward in the capital, and from sub-prefects and sub-circuit magistrates downward in the provinces, provided the regular route was not harmed.

京官中、行、評、博以下 names four capital offices (中書、行人、評事、博士) and all ranks below them; “up to … compilers” both truncates the list and reverses 以下. 同知、通判以下 is already rendered in this chapter as sub-prefects and sub-circuit magistrates, so the proposed switch to assistant prefects is unnecessary.

Once regulations opened, officials paid with stored grain; a tribute student buying immediate appointment as sub-prefect cost barely a thousand cash, a junior capital official only a few hundred—he requested requiring full payment in silver to stop abuses."

Once regulations opened, officials paid with stored grain; a tribute student buying immediate appointment as sub-prefect cost barely a thousand-odd taels, a junior capital official only a few hundred—he requested requiring full payment in silver to stop abuses."
千餘金 and 數百金 are silver-tael sums, set against 交銀. Rendering 金 as copper cash invents the wrong unit and blunts the abuse Zhang Guangsi is describing.

Once regulations were open, each official contributed with stored grain; calculating that a tribute student purchasing immediate-appointment sub-prefect cost no more than a thousand-odd in cash, and a junior capital official no more than several hundred, he requested ordering payment in silver at the full amount to stop abuses."

Once regulations were open, each official contributed with stored grain; calculating that a tribute student purchasing immediate-appointment sub-prefect cost no more than a thousand-odd taels, and a junior capital official no more than several hundred, he requested ordering payment in silver at the full amount to stop abuses."
The literal likewise turns 金 into cash. The surrounding 捐銀二十五兩 and 交銀 show the unit is silver taels.

Most regulations followed old practice; only the extended regulations allowed tribute licentiates to purchase Secretariat drafter posts, and the Henan works regulations allowed supplemental students to purchase educational posts.

Most regulations followed old practice; only the extended regulations allowed tribute licentiates to purchase Secretariat drafter posts, and the Henan works regulations allowed supplemental and attached students to purchase educational posts.
增、附捐教職 names two student statuses, zengsheng and fusheng. Dropping 附 omits attached students, whom the next sentence also pairs as 增、附.
In the thirteenth year, Wuzhi in Henan and the Qin and Yellow Rivers at Zhengzhou burst their banks.
In the thirteenth year, the Qin and Yellow Rivers burst their banks at Wuzhi and Zhengzhou in Henan.
河南武陟，鄭州沁、黃兩河漫決 locates Qin and Yellow River breaches at Wuzhi and Zhengzhou in Henan. The original literal makes Wuzhi itself burst beside the rivers.
Censors Zhou Tianlin and Li Shijin successively requested opening Zhengzhou river-works purchase regulations to fund urgent repairs.
Censors Zhou Tianlin and Li Shikun successively requested opening Zhengzhou river-works purchase regulations to fund urgent repairs.
李士錕 is Li Shikun (錕 = kun). Shijin does not match the given name 士錕.
Censors Zhou Tianlin and Li Shijin successively requested opening Zhengzhou works regulations to aid urgent projects.
Censors Zhou Tianlin and Li Shikun successively requested opening Zhengzhou works regulations to aid urgent projects.
The same given-name error appears in the literal field: 士錕 is Shikun, not Shijin.

Thereafter clerical officials from purchased-academy backgrounds seeking promotion or purchasing chief posts in the capital or provinces had first to purchase exemption from recommendation; only permitted-tribute graduates were exempt.

Thereafter, clerks and men of purchased-academy background who wished to be promoted or to purchase chief posts in the capital or provinces had first to purchase exemption from recommendation; only permitted-tribute graduates were exempt.
吏員例監出身者 is two origin routes, clerks and men of purchased-jiansheng background, not clerks who themselves came from the purchased academy.
During the Qianlong era regulations reopened repeatedly, but only for ordinary bi-monthly and monthly quotas—not the special prior-use or immediate-use categories.

During the Qianlong era regulations reopened repeatedly, but only for ordinary quota categories such as bi-monthly, monthly, regardless-of-bi-monthly selection, bi-monthly prior-use, and regardless-of-bi-monthly-or-monthly immediate-use.

惟 … 等尋常班次 includes the listed labels; 不論雙月選用, 雙月先用, and 不論雙、單月即用 are ordinary quota names, not English negation excluding prior-use and immediate-use. The proposed sentence is accurate but needs for to remain grammatical.
In the Qianlong years regulations were opened repeatedly, but only for bi-monthly and monthly ordinary quotas—not bi-monthly selection, bi-monthly prior use, or bi- and monthly immediate use.

In the Qianlong years regulations were opened repeatedly, but only ordinary quotas: bi-monthly, monthly, regardless-of-bi-monthly selection and bi-monthly prior-use, and regardless-of-bi-monthly-or-monthly immediate-use.
The literal field likewise treats 不論 as ‘not.’ In this list 不論 is part of the quota titles 不論雙月選用 and 不論雙、單月即用 under 尋常班次.
In Xianfeng 9, a succession of new quotas was established: new-quota vacancy, new-quota priority, split-vacancy priorities, and regardless-of-quota vacancy selection.

In Xianfeng 9, a succession of new quotas was established: new-quota vacancy, new-quota priority, split-vacancy pre-priority, split-vacancy inter-pre, full-quota pre-priority, and regardless-of-quota vacancy selection.
The Chinese enumerates six named quotas: 新班遇缺、新班侭先、分缺先前、分缺間前、本班侭先前、不論班侭遇缺選補. “Split-vacancy priorities” fuses and drops 分缺先前, 分缺間前, and 本班侭先前.
District magistrates had the regular route for supplementary appointment and were stingily not granted dispatch.
District magistrates, because they would obstruct supplementary appointment by the regular route, were stingily not granted dispatch.

有兒正途補用 is the character 礙 (石+兒) mis-encoded as 兒, i.e. 有礙正途補用. Gao Pu’s next sentence 恐有兒舉班 is already translated as fear of harming the juren quota. CText and Wikisource print the same 兒 graph; the sense is obstruction, not possession of the regular route.
That year the Ministry of War approved awaiting and candidate garrison commandants and company commanders purchasing dispatch and studying with grain transport, like civil officials.
That year the Ministry of War memorialized that awaiting and candidate garrison commandants and company commanders could purchase dispatch and study with grain transport, like civil officials.
是年兵部奏請 is a memorial requesting the measure. Approval comes only with 均報可 in the following sentences; saying the Ministry of War approved conflates petitioner and throne.

In Qianlong 46, awaiting registrars and candidate deputies petitioned the Ministry of Revenue: after long waits with no selection, provincial deputy quotas were clear—they requested purchase dispatch, and the old rule was restored.

In Qianlong 46, awaiting-appointment provincial administration registrar Zheng Zhaofang and others and candidate department assistant Zhang Yanling and others petitioned the Ministry of Revenue: after long waits with no selection, provincial deputy quotas were clear—they requested purchase dispatch, and the old rule was restored.
The Chinese names the petitioners 候補布政司經歷鄭肇芳等 and 候選州同張衍齡等. Omitting both names is a real loss of attribution already present in the literal field.

In Guangxu 8, Fujian-Zhejiang Governor He Jing reported: "Fujian examined 154 prefectural and county officials, 55 salt commissioners, and 596 deputies; prefects and salt commissioners were retained at fifty percent, sub-prefects and deputies at forty percent."

In Guangxu 8, Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General He Jing reported: "Fujian examined 154 prefectural and county officials, 55 salt commissioners, and 596 deputies; prefects and salt commissioners were retained at fifty percent, sub-prefects and deputies at forty percent."
閩浙總督 is the Min-Zhe governor-general, not a xunfu. Governor understates the office.
Thereafter tribute and academy examination for office was limited to department assistants, county assistants, registrars, and clerks.
Thereafter tribute and academy examination for office was limited to department assistants, department judges, county assistants, registrars, and clerks.
考職 posts are 州同、州判、縣丞、主簿、吏目. The original list drops 州判 (department judge).
When exposed, Wang Tanwang, Le Erjin, and Wang Tingzan were executed; dozens of officials were dismissed; contributors were barred from examinations, fined, or halted in selection.
When exposed, Wang Tanwang, Le Erjin, and Wang Tingzan were punished according to law; dozens of officials were dismissed; contributors were barred from examinations, fined, or halted in selection.
置亶望、勒爾謹、廷贊於法 means they were dealt with according to law. Execution is not stated here; the literal already has “punished by law.”
